intro.title: Welcome to FinTrack
intro.tagline: Incident tracking and traceability across FINSTAR branches.
intro.description: FinTrack lets you declare an incident, dispatch it to the right service, follow its life cycle in real time and guarantee end-to-end traceability for audits. It also produces operational reports about incidents and users within your access scope.
intro.audience: This guide targets every profile: agents, service heads, branch heads and administrators. Each section below describes the scope of available actions per role.

my_access.title: My access
my_access.intro: Here are the role and permissions attached to your account, and what they allow you to do in FinTrack.
my_access.no_roles: No role is attached to your account. Contact an administrator.
my_access.no_permissions: No permission is attached to your account. Contact an administrator.

creation.title: 1. Creation
creation.body: Anyone with the incident creation permission can declare an incident. Its initial status depends on the type configuration and the permission that allows direct opening; it can therefore be "Pending validation" or "Open".

validation.title: 2. Validation
validation.body: When validation is required, the incident is reviewed by the validator defined in its configuration: the agency manager or the target service manager. It can be validated or rejected with a reason.

transfer.title: 3. Transfer
transfer.body: The incident is routed to the target service configured for its type or selected by an authorized user. Assignment to a person then depends on the workflow rules and available permissions.

treatment.title: 4. Treatment
treatment.body: The responsible user takes the incident in hand: it becomes "In progress" while a solution is found and applied.

resolution.title: 5. Resolution
resolution.body: Once the solution is applied, the incident is marked "Resolved" with a resolution note.

closure.title: 6. Closure
closure.body: The resolved incident is closed: it becomes "Closed", finished and archived. A resolution description is required.

reopen.title: 7. Reopening
reopen.body: A rejected incident can be reopened for correction. A resolved incident resumes processing when reopened; a closed incident must be cloned.

viewAndFilter.title: View and filter
viewAndFilter.body: Switch between the Table and Cards views as you prefer. Use the search bar and filters (type, status, criticality, period) to find a specific incident, and the quick filters to hide closed/rejected/cancelled incidents or show only unassigned ones. An administrator can also narrow the list to a given agency or service.

create.title: Create an incident
create.body: Incidents page, "New incident" button. Fill in at least the title, description, type and criticality. Your account must be attached to an agency.

edit.title: Edit an incident
edit.body: Incidents that are "Open", "Pending validation" or "Reopened" can be edited when your permission and the workflow rules allow it.

validate.title: Validate an incident
validate.body: An authorized user validates an incident within the scope defined by its configuration. The system checks the permission, agency and, when required, target service.

reject.title: Reject an incident
reject.body: An incident deemed invalid is rejected with a mandatory reason, which the creator can then review.

transfer.title: Transfer an incident
transfer.body: Transferring routes the incident to the responsible service. Depending on your role, a transfer reason may be required.

assign.title: Assign an incident
assign.body: An incident can be assigned to a specific user in charge of handling it.

resolve.title: Resolve an incident
resolve.body: The user in charge applies a solution and enters a resolution note.

close.title: Close an incident
close.body: Closing finalizes the incident. A resolution description is required.

reopen.title: Reopen an incident
reopen.body: Rejected incidents can be reopened for correction. Closed incidents are cloned instead of reopened.

delete.title: Delete an incident
delete.body: Incident deletion is currently disabled in the interface to preserve traceability. Incidents remain available according to your permissions.

overview.title: Overview
overview.body: The incident page gathers the title, description, type, criticality, status, scope, responsible users, dates and deadline information visible within your scope.

attachments.title: Attachments
attachments.body: Attachments document the incident. Check their content before submitting and open them from the incident page when your access allows it.

comments.title: Comments and exchanges
comments.body: Authorized users can add comments to clarify the analysis, request information or record decisions related to the incident.

history.title: History
history.body: The history keeps status changes, validations, transfers, assignments and other actions so that processing remains verifiable.

clone.title: Clone an incident
clone.body: A closed incident is not edited: a user with the creation permission can clone it to handle a similar new case and review the data before submitting.

fields.title: Field guide (incident form)
fields.intro: Explanation of each field in the incident creation/modification form.

types.title: Incident Types
types.intro: Incident types define the category of the problem and generally determine which service it will be transferred to. Here are the types currently configured in the system:

causes.title: Incident Causes
causes.intro: When resolving an incident, you must categorize its root cause. Here are the definitions:

statuses.title: Incident statuses
statuses.intro: The statuses below come directly from the system and reflect the stage of each incident.

criticality.title: Criticality levels
criticality.intro: Criticality indicates the urgency and impact of an incident.

roles.title: Roles & permissions
roles.intro: The list of roles comes from the system: any role added by an administrator appears here automatically.

overview.title: Overview
overview.body: The dashboard gives a synthetic, up-to-date view of incident activity: key counters, distribution by type and criticality, rankings and evolution trends. It is your entry point to steer activity at a glance.

kpis.title: Key indicators
kpis.body: The indicators (open, pending, resolved, closed, total incidents...) summarize the current state. Each value is compared with the previous period, with a variation that immediately flags an improvement or a degradation.

period.title: Period selection
period.body: The period selector (today, 7 days, 30 days, this month, custom range...) recomputes all statistics over the chosen interval, to analyze a trend or a specific moment.

scope.title: Scope
scope.body: All data is limited to your authorization scope: your incidents, those of your service, your agency, or the entire system. An administrator can additionally filter by a specific agency, service or user.

stockFlow.title: Stock and flow
stockFlow.body: Stock indicators describe the current situation, while flow indicators count actions completed during the selected period. Always read the period together with the selected scope.

configPanel.title: Configuration
configPanel.body: The configuration panel (settings icon) customizes your dashboard: show or hide widgets and reorder their layout. Your preferences are saved for your next visits.

what.title: What you receive
what.body: You are notified of incidents you created, those assigned to you and status changes within your scope.

channels.title: Channels
channels.body: Notifications appear in the application and may be sent by email. A browser system notification is offered when it is authorized.

browser.title: Browser notifications
browser.body: To receive alerts while FinTrack is not in the foreground, preferably use Chrome and allow notifications for the FinTrack address in the browser settings.

when.title: When
when.body: Recipients depend on the event and permissions: the creator, assigned user, validator, concerned managers and administrators may be notified. Clicking a notification opens the related item when it remains accessible.

generate.title: Generate a report
generate.body: Produce an incident report over a given period and scope.

schedule.title: Schedule a report
schedule.body: Schedule automatic, recurring report generation. The sending time follows the timezone configured by the system environment.

formats.title: Formats & export
formats.body: Reports can be exported and, if enabled, emailed to recipients.

email.title: Email delivery
email.body: Email delivery is available only with the corresponding permission and a valid email configuration. Check recipients before sending.

delete.title: Delete a report
delete.body: Reports can be deleted only when your permission allows it. This removes the generated report, not the incidents used to produce it.

scope.title: Scope
scope.body: A report's content is limited to your access scope (your incidents, service, agency or the whole system).

info.title: My information
info.body: View and update your personal information: name, email, phone.

password.title: Password
password.body: On first login the temporary password must be changed. You can then change it at any time.

rolesPermissions.title: Roles & permissions
rolesPermissions.body: Your profile shows your roles and permissions. The screens and sections available in FinTrack depend on effective permissions, not only on the role label.

incidentTypes.title: Incident types
incidentTypes.body: Define incident types, their processing deadline and their default target service or responsible user.

agencies.title: Agencies
agencies.body: Manage the organization's agencies and their head.

services.title: Services
services.body: Manage the agencies' internal services and their service head.

rolesPerm.title: Roles & permissions
rolesPerm.body: Create roles and adjust the permissions granted to each.

reportSchedules.title: Report schedules
reportSchedules.body: View, create and edit schedules according to your permission. Check the scope, period, format, recipients and timezone before activation.

system.title: System
system.body: Access the general settings and transfer rules of the system.

view.title: View users
view.body: The list and details displayed depend on your viewing scope: service, agency or all users.

create.title: Create a user
create.body: You only see account types that your permissions allow you to create. Check the agency, service, role and status before confirming.

permissions.title: Roles and permissions
permissions.body: Role or permission assignment is offered only to authorized users. A custom role must explicitly receive the permissions needed for its activities.

status.title: Status and profile
status.body: Changing a user's status and information depends on the management permissions available within your scope.

view.title: Audit log
view.body: The log presents actions visible within your scope. The export includes available information such as the author, action, resource, identifier, IP address and result.

selfAssign.q: How do I assign an incident directly to myself?
selfAssign.a: Tick "Assign this incident to me" in the create form. This option is always available and takes precedence over any other configuration: the incident is assigned directly to you, with no transfer to the service imposed by the type.

targetService.q: Why is the « Target Service » field sometimes disabled?
targetService.a: It is disabled when the incident type already enforces a service, or when you have checked « Assign this incident to me » — in which case the incident is directly assigned to you.

autoFill.q: Why are the « Agency » and « Service » fields disabled when creating a user?
autoFill.a: As an agency or service manager, you can only create users within your own scope. These fields are therefore automatically pre-filled for you.

notifications.a: On the creation and assignment of an incident, and on status changes within your scope — in the application and, if an email address is configured, by email.

editIncident.q: Why can I no longer edit an incident?
editIncident.a: Only "Open" or "Pending validation" incidents are editable. As soon as an incident is validated or processed, its content is frozen.

deletedAudit.q: What happens to a deleted item?
deletedAudit.a: Incident deletion is disabled to preserve traceability. Reports and users remain subject to their respective management permissions.

firstLogin.q: Why must I change my password on first login?
firstLogin.a: Your account is created with a temporary password. For security reasons, you must set your own password on first login.

title.label: Title
title.help: Short, clear summary of the incident (3 to 200 characters).

description.label: Description
description.help: Detailed description of the problem: context, symptoms, impact (up to 5000 characters).

type.label: Incident type
type.help: Category of the incident. The type may impose a target service or responsible user and define a processing deadline.

criticality.label: Criticality
criticality.help: Level of urgency and impact. A critical incident notifies every administrator.

dueDate.label: Due date
dueDate.help: Processing deadline. It is computed automatically from the deadline configured for the incident type.

incidentDate.label: Incident date
incidentDate.help: Actual occurrence date of the event; it may be earlier than the creation date.

observationDate.label: Observation date
observationDate.help: Date the incident was observed; defaults to today.

targetService.label: Target service
targetService.help: Service the incident should be routed to. Disabled if the type imposes a service or if self-assignment is ticked.

assignToSelf.label: Assign this incident to me
assignToSelf.help: Assigns the incident directly to you. Always available, this option takes precedence over the routing imposed by the type.

cause.label: Cause
cause.help: Main cause of the incident (optional at creation): human, technical, external, etc.

causeDetail.label: Cause detail
causeDetail.help: Detail about the cause: responsible person or detailed description, depending on the chosen cause.

attachments.label: Attachments
attachments.help: Documents or screenshots completing the incident. Added in the form, they are uploaded after creation.

statuses_catalog.DRAFT: The handler has submitted an intervention solution to Executive Management. The incident awaits approval before processing can continue; the deadline keeps running during this wait.
statuses_catalog.OPEN: The incident has just been reported and is awaiting handling. No processing action has taken place yet: it is the starting point of the lifecycle.
statuses_catalog.PENDING_VALIDATION: Reported by an agent, the incident awaits approval by a validator (agency or target-service manager) before it can move forward. The validator can approve it or reject it with a reason.
statuses_catalog.VALIDATED: The incident has been approved: it is recognized as admissible and ready to be routed to the responsible service.
statuses_catalog.TRANSFERRED: The incident has been routed to the competent service and awaits assignment to a handler there.
statuses_catalog.ASSIGNED: A specific handler has been designated to process the incident, but processing has not started yet.
statuses_catalog.IN_PROGRESS: A handler has taken charge of the incident and is actively working on its resolution. This processing phase is tracked against the deadline.
statuses_catalog.BLOCKED: Processing is temporarily suspended (dependency, missing information...). The deadline, however, keeps running.
statuses_catalog.RESOLVED: A solution has been applied and documented with a resolution note. The incident awaits an official closure to be definitively finished.
statuses_catalog.CLOSED: The incident is definitively finished and archived, with a closure summary. This is a final, non-editable state (a copy can be created if the problem reappears).
statuses_catalog.REOPENED: A previously rejected incident has been reopened for correction and re-enters the processing flow.
statuses_catalog.REJECTED: The incident was deemed inadmissible and refused, with a mandatory reason visible to the creator. It can be reopened for correction.
statuses_catalog.UNRESOLVED_PROLONGED_WAIT: The incident remained blocked beyond the configured maximum duration and requires intervention or closer follow-up. It remains unresolved, but standard deadline reminders are suspended in this state.

criticality_catalog.LOW: Minor, localized impact. Handling follows the normal course, with no particular urgency.
criticality_catalog.MEDIUM: Moderate impact on activity. To be handled quickly to prevent the situation from worsening.
criticality_catalog.HIGH: Significant impact: part of the activity is disrupted. Prompt, priority handling is expected.
criticality_catalog.CRITICAL: Severe or blocking impact on activity. Absolute urgency: all administrators are notified immediately.

causes_catalog.HUMAN: Human error: mishandling, oversight, incorrect entry, or lack of training. Choose this when the origin is a person's action (or inaction).
causes_catalog.TECHNICAL: Technical failure: hardware breakdown, software bug, network unavailability, or a business application (CBS...) being down.
causes_catalog.ORGANIZATIONAL: Organizational cause: unsuitable process, poor communication between teams, or lack of resources.
causes_catalog.ENVIRONMENTAL: Environmental cause: power outage, weather incident, extreme temperature, or any physical factor external to the information system.
causes_catalog.EXTERNAL: External cause: failure of a provider or partner, or a malicious action (cyberattack, fraud).
causes_catalog.STRUCTURAL: Structural cause: architecture limit, system design flaw, or undersized infrastructure.
causes_catalog.OTHER: Cause that does not fall into any category above. A written description of the cause is then required.

roles_catalog.AGENT: Creates incidents and views their own.
roles_catalog.CHEF_SERVICE: Handles, resolves and closes the incidents of their service.
roles_catalog.CHEF_AGENCE: Validates and transfers incidents, manages the agents of their agency.
roles_catalog.ADMIN: Full system management, except acting on a Super Admin account.
roles_catalog.SUPER_ADMIN: Full access; only the Super Admin can act on their own account.

permissions.INCIDENT_UPDATE: Edit an incident still open or pending validation.
permissions.INCIDENT_REOPEN: Reopen a rejected or resolved incident.
permissions.INCIDENT_VIEW_SERVICE: View the incidents of your service.
permissions.INCIDENT_VIEW_AGENCY: View the incidents of your agency.
permissions.INCIDENT_VIEW_ALL: View every incident in the system.
permissions.INCIDENT_TRANSFER: Transfer an incident to a service.
permissions.INCIDENT_AUTO_TRANSFER: Benefit from automatic transfer based on the incident type.
permissions.INCIDENT_TRANSFER_WITH_REASON: Transfer an incident while providing a reason.
permissions.INCIDENT_TREAT: Take in hand and process incidents.
permissions.INCIDENT_CANCEL: Cancel an incident while no handler is assigned.
permissions.INCIDENT_REJECT: Reject an incident with a reason.
permissions.INCIDENT_DELETE: Delete an incident not yet processed.
permissions.REPORT_VIEW_SERVICE: View the reports of your service.
permissions.REPORT_VIEW_AGENCY: View the reports of your agency.
permissions.USER_CREATE_ALL_AGENT: Create agent accounts in any scope.
permissions.USER_CREATE_AGENT_AGENCY: Create agent accounts in the user's agency.
permissions.USER_CREATE_AGENT_SERVICE: Create agent accounts in the user's service.
permissions.USER_VIEW_SERVICE: View the users of your service.
permissions.USER_VIEW_AGENCY: View the users of your agency.
permissions.USER_MANAGE_PROFILE: View and edit your own profile.
permissions.ROLE_ASSIGN: Assign roles and permissions to users.
